passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute
passages.note: House engrossed text of the same record; the pre-substitution title is inside a [deleted: ] fence and is not the provision.

rows.reasoning: His only act here is a Y on SCR1040 (2024), which would let an employer of a tipped worker "pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute" so long as tips bring the worker to the minimum plus $2. That is a carve-out for one group of workers, not a position on the general floor: it neither "Hold[s] the wage floor at its current level and let[s] the market set pay above it" nor "Remove[s] the wage floor entirely", since the measure keeps a statutory floor and a guaranteed make-up amount. It shows a side without separating the rungs on that side.
